lens: Statistics and inference. What does the evidence actually license? Transfer by class as an assumption rather than a measurement; effect sizes against their own uncertainty; whether every control could have failed; multiplicity; absence claims stated at the strength the method supports; whether any comparison exceeds what n can carry.
what_i_read: research/manuscripts/dependency/emc-atr-vulnerability-assessment.md @ 2401803d2 (1,036 lines, 14,361 words) — the pinned document, read in full

research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py @ 2401803d2 — the producing module; part B scoring and contrasts (l.2010-2110), part B pooling and cuts (l.2280-2345), part C (l.2440-2600), part D specificity and mechanism tests (l.2840-2990), grade() (l.2988-3040), _spearman (l.370-390)

central_claim: In public data the FET-fusion -> impaired-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency hypothesis grades WEAK for EMC: EMC tumours' DDR transcripts are elevated no further than their generic proliferation on two independent series; the CRISPR knockout readout is saturated and cannot discriminate; and of four pre-registered mechanism tests in GDSC2 only one passes, and that one is a statement about the drug rather than about EMC. The vulnerability itself is inherited from a class on which the mechanism was measured in other diseases, and nothing computed here changes that.

blockers.quote: What the tier *is*, is a bound on three sides now instead of two: no coordinated dependency, no sensitivity tracking ATM status, and no proliferation-independent DDR signature in EMC tumours.
blockers.summary: Two of the three named 'sides' are readings from instruments this document itself declares incapable of bearing on the hypothesis, so the sentence converts two failed instruments into evidence against the hypothesis, four lines after saying the hypothesis is neither supported nor refuted.
blockers.evidence: Side 1, 'no coordinated dependency', is part C. §4 closes: 'Reported as a failed instrument, and it must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis. ... This readout can support the hypothesis or miss it. It cannot refute it.' The artifact agrees — part_c_coordinated_dependency.verdict = 'INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND', verdict_reading = '...this instrument cannot support OR refute a selective ATR-axis dependency in FET-fusion lines.' Side 2, 'no sensitivity tracking ATM status', is part D's ATM row, whose predictor is expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair — transcript abundance. The same §6.1 paragraph, two sentences earlier, says: 'The mechanism is a recruitment-and-phosphorylation event at a double-strand break; nothing in an expression matrix can measure it, so a cell with entirely normal DDR transcript levels can still have a defective ATM response.' Only side 3 (part B, the transcriptional shadow) is a bound the method supports, and §6.1 correctly scopes that one to the shadow. A bound is a partial refutation; the paragraph says in one sentence that no refutation exists and in the next that three of them do. The §6.1 predicate table already prints the honest version of side 1 — 'no — instrument blind (§4)' — so the contradiction is internal to one subsection.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Any restatement that keeps 'bound on three sides' while §4's 'it must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis' stands. The two are not reconcilable by hedging the surrounding prose; one of the three sides has to be withdrawn or re-described as an absent reading rather than a null. This is the same distinction the document builds the NOT_ASSESSABLE tier to enforce for part B (§1, §3.3) and then does not enforce for part C in the grading section.

blockers.where: THE HEADLINE (lines 88-91) and §5 throughout; propagated to §6.1's predicate row and to §6.3
blockers.quote: The mechanism's *load-bearing* prediction — **low ATM signalling marks ATRi sensitivity** — comes back at rho = **-0.090**, the **wrong sign** ... [§5] The published mechanism's central variable is still the variable that leaves no trace in this data, on direction and magnitude alike.
blockers.summary: The mechanism's central variable is ATM activation at a double-strand break. It is operationalised here as ATM-pathway transcript abundance, and the failure of that proxy is reported as a fact about the mechanism. §5 nowhere states that an expression matrix cannot observe the variable — and §3.4 attributes that limit TO §5, where it does not exist.
blockers.evidence: grep -n -E 'phosphoryl|recruitment' over the pinned document returns lines 120 (headline, pointing at §6.1), 489 (oxidative phosphorylation, unrelated), 529 (§3.4), 723 (§6.1) and 769 (§6.3). §5 runs from line 590 to line 705 (§6 opens at 706) and contains none of them. Line 529, inside §3.4, reads: 'Section 5's limit applies with full force here: the mechanism is a protein recruitment and phosphorylation event at a double-strand break, and no expression matrix can show it.' — attributing to §5 a limit §5 does not carry. Part B's identical instrument gets the caveat in full and part D's does not, and part D is where the document declares the mechanism not to track. The predictor really is expression: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity['expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair'], mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors = -0.0903, computed from DepMap OmicsExpression log2(TPM+1) over the Reactome DNA Double Strand Break Response set. §5's table row is labelled 'ATM-signalling expression', which is a label rather than a caveat; the headline drops even that. The honest reading of the row is that the instrument cannot see the variable, which is a different finding from the prediction being contradicted — and it changes what §6.1's predicate 'ATR-inhibitor sensitivity tracks the mechanism | no' is a 'no' about.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Restoring 'the wrong sign' as a claim about the mechanism while §6.1 and §3.4 continue to say no expression matrix can measure this event. The fix is one sentence in §5 stating that ATM-pathway transcript level is not ATM signalling capacity, and a correction to §3.4's cross-reference; the headline then has to say the proxy leaves no trace rather than that the prediction comes back wrong. The four bars, the numbers and the 1-of-4 verdict are all untouched by it.

p1s.summary: The single passing test has no same-modality negative control. Nothing in part D tests whether ANY strong CRISPR dependency score correlates with the ATR-inhibitor residual, so 'ATR-axis dependency predicts ATRi sensitivity' is not separated from 'dependency scores in general predict drug-specific residuals'.
p1s.evidence: part_d_drug_response_correlation.correlations carries 10 predictors x 7 drugs = 70 Spearman correlations. Exactly one predictor is a dependency score: dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1_mean_gene_effect. Its two specificity bars compare it against EXPRESSION predictors (expr::proliferation_MYC at rho -0.1711) and against non-DDR DRUGS (paclitaxel +0.007, bortezomib +0.0213). No pan-essential or unrelated-gene dependency predictor exists. The module's own comment concedes the cross-modal problem — 'a dependency predictor is on a different scale and sign from an expression predictor, so the comparison is on |rho| and is only meaningful as "is this bigger than growth rate"' — and the paper reproduces the scale caveat once, in its standard-error sentence. The missing control is free: RPL5 (-2.7439) and PLK1 (-2.7148) gene effects are already computed and cached in the SAME artifact, part_c_coordinated_dependency.per_gene, and part D already reads CRISPRGeneEffect. A pan-essential dependency score correlated against the same seven drugs is the one comparison that would tell a reader whether the passing row is about ATR or about line fitness — which is the document's own thesis for everything else it reports.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing in the text; the gap is in the analysis. Absent that control, §5's '✅ What passes, and why it is worth something' has to state that the passing predictor's negative control is cross-modal and that no dependency-modality null was run.

p1s.where: §3.4, the sentence carrying part B's conclusion; repeated in §6.1's predicate table
p1s.quote: Three DDR concepts clear the raw threshold and none survives the proliferation adjustment — and the two *unrelated* control sets (oxphos, adipogenesis) move as much as or more than any DDR set. That is the signature of a growth-rate difference, not of a DDR mechanism.
p1s.summary: False for one of the two controls, and refuted by the table eight lines above it. Only oxphos exceeds every DDR set; adipogenesis is exceeded by three of them. The 'growth rate, not DDR' reading is carried by one control, not two.
p1s.evidence: From per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz'].contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma, raw delta_a_minus_b: control_adipogenesis +0.2183, against ATR_CHK1_activity +0.2451, DNA_damage_checkpoint +0.2564 and S_phase_E2F +0.3111. control_oxphos +0.3843 does exceed all six DDR concepts. The paper prints all of these numbers in its own §3.4 table. On the proliferation-adjusted scale the gap widens: adipogenesis +0.0353 against S_phase_E2F +0.1282 and DNA_damage_checkpoint +0.0735. §6.1 restates it as 'two unrelated control sets move as much (§3.4)'. Read charitably as 'at least as much as SOME DDR set' the sentence is true and vacuous; in the position it occupies, immediately before 'That is the signature of a growth-rate difference', it is doing the work of 'at least as much as ALL of them', and that is false for adipogenesis on both scales.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any restatement that keeps both controls in the comparison. The claim that survives is the one-control version — oxidative phosphorylation, an unrelated control, moves further than every DDR concept — plus the adjustment result, which stands on its own.

p1s.where: §6.1, and §3.4's 'it does not matter here, because the two series agree'
p1s.quote: The verbatim WEAK criterion is *"only generic proliferation/DNA-damage genes are elevated"*, and that is precisely what two independent EMC series show.
p1s.summary: The graded predicate reads ONE series. On the other, nothing at all clears the elevation cut — DDR, proliferation and controls alike — so the WEAK criterion's own words are not instantiated there, and the module's verdict for that series alone would be the string §3.3 records as the near-published failure.
p1s.evidence: part_b_emc_tumour_signature.platforms_with_a_readable_EMC_vs_comparator_contrast = ['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz'], a single entry, and every row of pooled_raw_contrast carries n_platforms: 1. GSE24369 appears in readable_platforms_in_ANY_series and contributes to no predicate. Run the module's own cut over GSE24369's contrasts: the largest |delta| across all twelve concepts is control_oxphos +0.1131; proliferation_MYC is +0.0844 and no DDR concept exceeds +0.0445. Nothing reaches 0.2, so ddr_concepts_elevated_raw would be empty, signature_present would be False, and derive_part_b's first branch would set verdict = 'NO_DDR_SIGNATURE_IN_EMC_TUMOURS' with the reading 'that is a readable negative, and it is evidence against the transfer' — the exact sentence §3.3 records as the failure the module exists to prevent — rather than 'GENERIC_ONLY'. grade() would still land on WEAK, but through its final else branch ('the grading's leading predicate fails'), not through the 'only generic ... elevated' branch. So the two series reach the same tier by different routes and do not show the same thing; and §3.4's 'it does not matter here, because the two series agree', which is what defuses the rank-key choice, is weaker than stated. This matters because the series the rank key DID pick is the one §3.4 itself calls 'not the better instrument' and the one carrying the undetermined reference-channel confound.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Keeping 'precisely what two independent EMC series show'. The supported version is that GSE24369 is flat at every concept including the generic ones, which is consistent with the WEAK reading and is not an instance of it.

p1s.quote: [§8.4] SARC-HRD would not select it at all if EMC is HR-proficient as its class is measured to be. ... [§8.2] If EMC behaves as its class does — HR-proficient, per the source paper's own measurement on the FET class —
p1s.summary: Both sentences assert a class-level measurement of HR status. §8.5, thirty lines later, denies it: the measurement was on Ewing tumours. Measured on one member, asserted of the class — the elision the banner exists to forbid, inside the section that draws the adverse consequence for route 1.
p1s.evidence: §8.5 point 1 reads in full: 'That EMC is HR-proficient. Not measured here. The source paper measured it for *Ewing* tumours, and EMC's HR status is unknown in public data.' The preprint quotations §8.2 itself reproduces are all scoped to ES: 'ES patient tumors do not display the genomic scars of HR deficiency', 'EWSR1-FLI1 does not induce isolated HR deficiency', 'ES tumors are not "BRCA-like", but instead harbor partial ATM defects'. The only class-level statement in the quoted material is a NOMINATION — 'identify the compensatory ATR signaling axis as a synthetic lethal therapeutic strategy for the class of FET rearranged cancers' — which is a claim by the authors, not a measurement across the class. The banner's own rule applies verbatim: the mechanism 'was measured on other FET fusions in other diseases', and class inheritance is not a measurement.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any wording that keeps 'as its class is measured to be' or 'measurement on the FET class'. The supported form is 'as measured in Ewing', which is what §8.5 already says and which weakens neither of §8.4's three findings — none of them needs EMC to be HR-proficient, only that its HR status is unknown.

p2s.summary: Multiplicity is not mentioned anywhere in the document, and the number of comparisons made is never stated. It does not change a verdict, and the one positive result survives a Bonferroni over the full count — but neither of those two facts is told to the reader either.
p2s.evidence: Part D computes 70 (drug x predictor) Spearman correlations — 10 predictors over 7 drugs, from part_d_drug_response_correlation.correlations, of which only 4 predictors are the pre-registered mechanism tests. Part B computes roughly 96 Welch contrasts (12 concepts x 4 contrast blocks x 2 readable platforms), part C 14. No word of the family 'multiple comparison / Bonferroni / FDR / familywise' appears in the document. The verdicts are structurally immune, because every cut is an effect-size cut applied with 'no significance requirement' (§1) — that is a real defence and it is not stated as one. And the passing test survives correction comfortably: ceralasertib t 6.352 at n 597 gives p = 4.2e-10, berzosertib t 4.157 at n 565 gives p = 3.7e-5, against a Bonferroni alpha of 0.05/70 = 7.1e-4. So does MK-1775 (t 3.893, n 601, p = 1.1e-4), which sharpens rather than softens §5's own 'no bar in this analysis separates ATR from a neighbouring checkpoint kinase'. As printed, a reader meets t = 5.08, 5.92, 3.89 and 6.35 with no idea how many tests they were drawn from.

p2s.summary: The proliferation-adjusted column decides part B's verdict and is printed with no uncertainty at all, while the raw column, which decides nothing, carries t. The artifact holds an adjusted Welch t for every concept, and three of the omitted numbers are informative — one of them is the strongest single datum for the paper's own conclusion.
p2s.evidence: §3.4's table prints raw delta with t and prints the adjusted column as a bare number; the controls' adjusted values are printed as '—'. From contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma_PROLIFERATION_ADJUSTED on GPL3290: S_phase_E2F +0.1282 (t 3.602, df 10.7) and DNA_damage_checkpoint +0.0735 (t 2.378, df 12.7) remain non-null after the adjustment, while control_adipogenesis falls to +0.0353 (t 1.017) — and control_oxphos stays at +0.2014, which CLEARS the paper's own 0.2 elevation cut after the proliferation adjustment. That last number is the cleanest evidence in the artifact for 'a growth-rate difference, not a DDR mechanism' and it is absent from the document. Nothing here moves a verdict — the elevation cut is explicitly effect-size-only, so no rule is broken — but the deciding column is the one shown without its error, in a paper that is otherwise scrupulous about exactly this (§5's '0.41x that standard error').

p2s.summary: Part C's blindness gate can classify a statistically detectable coordinated dependency as an instrument failure, because it compares a difference of MEANS against a per-line SD rather than against the standard error of that difference — and it short-circuits the branch that would have reported support.
p2s.evidence: In emc_atr_vulnerability.py, blind = (axis_mean_sarcoma_pool < -1.0 and abs(delta) < axis_sd_sarcoma_pool), evaluated BEFORE 'elif joint_delta < 0 and joint_t < -2: verdict = COORDINATED_DEPENDENCY_SUPPORTED'. With the observed values — axis_sd_sarcoma_pool = 0.1904, n_FET = 20, n_matched = 71 — SE(delta) = 0.1904 * sqrt(1/20 + 1/71) = 0.0482. The blindness gate therefore holds until |t| = 3.95, while the support branch opens at |t| = 2. Any effect with 2 < |t| < 3.95 — Cohen's d roughly 0.5 to 1.0, an ordinary detectable group difference — is reported as 'INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND' rather than as support. No reported verdict is affected: the observed delta is -0.0065, t = -0.13, nowhere near either boundary. What is affected is §4's claim 'This readout can support the hypothesis or miss it' and the reachability of the STRONG tier, which requires grade()'s dep_selective, which requires the shadowed branch. As constructed, the readout can support the hypothesis only at d > 1.

p2s.summary: §4's 'The controls pass' has no criterion that could have failed. The controls do recover their expected values, so the reading is correct — what is missing is a rule. §8.3, in the same document, shows exactly how it should be done.
p2s.evidence: derive_part_c emits ATM, RPL5 and PLK1 per-gene rows and no pass predicate; part_c_coordinated_dependency in the artifact carries no control verdict and no threshold. The values do recover — ATM FET_sarcoma_only_mean -0.0344 with frac_dependent_panel_wide 0.007, RPL5 -2.7439 with 1.000 — so §4's reading is right on the numbers. Contrast §8.3, where atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py sets an explicit _pass_condition with absolute cuts (ACTB and GAPDH median > 100 TPM, ALB and INS median < 5 TPM), computes state = PASS/FAIL from them, and gates the whole section behind 'if instrument_controls.state != PASS: verdict = CANNOT_DETERMINE'. That control could fail; part C's cannot, because nothing is asked of it. Also unprinted: PLK1, a second pan-essential control at -2.7148 / 0.999, is computed and does not appear in §4's table — and it sits BELOW the hypothesis gene WEE1 (-2.5997, frac 1.000), which is the plainest available demonstration that the axis is saturated.

p2s.summary: §4's key sentence reads as its own opposite against the table three lines above it.
p2s.evidence: 'A readout on which essentially nothing is negative cannot discriminate' sits directly under a table in which every gene effect is a negative number and 99.2-100 % of lines are 'dependent' (gene effect below -0.5). The intended sense is 'no line is a non-dependent NEGATIVE in the assay-control sense'; the printed sense is the reverse of the table. ATM, at frac_dependent 0.007, is the one gene for which the statement is literally true and it is a control rather than a hypothesis gene.

p2s.summary: §0's 'what still stands' calls four items 'structural arguments from sequence' that 'do not depend on a public-data correlation at any point'. The RGG dose-calibration prediction is not one: it maps a sequence RG count onto a measured recruitment series from other fusions in other diseases — a class transfer wearing the label the banner reserves for sequence.
p2s.evidence: emc-fet-construct-designs.json -> rgg_dose_calibration_and_predictions._the_calibration_curve_is_theirs_not_ours: 'The source built an RGG dose series into EWSR1-FLI1 and into EWSR1-ATF1 and measured recruitment for each ... That series is the axis; the EMC constructs are placed ON it'. The document's own defence in the table's second column — 'it uses their calibration, not ours' — says whose correlation it is, not that the step is not one. And the axis has two usable anchors: source_anchors carries EWSR1-FLI1 at fraction_of_wildtype_RG 0.0 and EWSR1-RGG(3)-FLI1 at 1.0, with the intermediate EWSR1-RGG(1)-FLI1 recorded as ewsr1_RG_retained: null, fraction_of_wildtype_RG: null. So EMC is interpolated between two endpoints with no measured intermediate. The sibling artifact is honest about the consequence and registers only ORDINAL predictions with 'No effect size is predicted'; the pinned document's one-line table row carries neither the class-transfer step nor the two-anchor limit.

p2s.summary: §0 reports EMC's commonest fusion at less than the weight its own producing artifact gives it, and 'bracket the retained-RG axis' overstates the span.
p2s.evidence: §0 says type 1 'keeps 8 of 30 — a weaker, non-identical match to the measured construct', graded against one control (the Ewing type-1 construct at 0/30). On the RGG axis the producing artifact places type 1 (0.267) exactly among the EWSR1::ATF1 types in which the mechanism was measured and found present: emc-fet-idr-census.json -> positive_controls['EWSR1::ATF1 ...'] carries e8 at 7/30 = 0.233 and e10 at 8/30 = 0.267, and emc-fet-construct-designs.json's registered prediction P2 says so in terms — 'against 7 of 30 for EWSR1::ATF1 at EWSR1 exon 8 and 8 of 30 at exon 10 — the clear-cell types in which this mechanism was MEASURED and found present'. Separately, 'bracket the retained-RG axis' brackets the measured RANGE, not the axis, which runs to 1.0 (the engineered RGG(3) construct); and a third EMC type in the same artifact, type 5 at 11/30 = 0.367, sits above both and is not mentioned. Related, and out of this document's scope but load-bearing for §0's citation: the census's own comparative block still keys EMC as emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3 with last_fet_residue_retained 264 and emc_RG_retained_fraction 0.0 in every row of emc_vs_measured_fusions_comparative, concluding holds_against_every_measured_type: true — i.e. the census computes its headline comparison on the fusion this document's Appendix says is the SECOND-commonest, and that comparison would be false for the commonest one (0.267 exceeds three of the four measured types' fractions and ties the fourth). The prose correction the Appendix records reached §0 and did not reach the artifact §0 cites.

p2s.summary: §6.1's '16 EMC tumours' sums two series that the producing module refuses to pool. No contrast anywhere in the document is computed on 16 samples.
p2s.evidence: The verdict-carrying contrast is 10 EMC vs 6 comparators (GPL3290 class_counts: EMC 10, GIST 3, DFSP 3); the corroborating one is 6 EMC vs 29 (GSE24369). The module's own comment at the series-selection step reads 'POOLING ACROSS SERIES WOULD BE A CATEGORY ERROR, and it is the one new way a multi-series part B could lie', and the artifact guards the same summation explicitly: _class_counts_scope = 'every platform of every series read — a census, NOT a group size. The group sizes the verdict rests on are in series_readability...'. '16 EMC tumours' is that forbidden sum, printed as part B's sample size in the grading section.

p2s.summary: §5's one reassurance about the passing test is itself a bar cleared by half a standard error — in the paragraph whose whole point is that such a margin is not a margin.
p2s.evidence: After conceding that the passing test's proliferation bar is cleared by 0.41 SE, §5 adds: 'Its direction and its |rho| >= 0.15 bar are untouched — both drugs clear 0.15 separately.' Per drug: ceralasertib rho +0.252 at n 597 clears 0.15 by 0.102 = 2.49 SE (SE = 1/sqrt(n-3) = 0.0410); berzosertib rho +0.1726 at n 565 clears it by 0.0226 = 0.54 SE (SE = 0.0422). So one of the two drugs clears the magnitude floor by roughly half its own standard error. The bar as coded is on the mean across ATR inhibitors (magnitude_at_least_0.15 reads mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors = 0.2123, which clears by 1.6 SE of a single rho and more of the mean's own), so no verdict moves — but the sentence's per-drug form is offered as the robustness that survives the SE concession, and for berzosertib it does not survive it. The document says two lines later, correctly, 'Nothing here rests on a difference this document measured an interval for, because it measured none.'

where_the_paper_survives: §1's falsifiable pre-registration claim — 'None of the three has been changed since it was written, which is checkable in the module's git history' — CHECKS OUT. git log -L over the elevated-delta block (l.2317-2325), over the atri_specific bar (l.2916-2918), over the beats_the_proliferation_control bar (l.2935-2936) and over the passes/tracks_mechanism block (l.2963-2975) each return exactly one commit, 5c2b04157, dated 2026-08-05. git log -S on 'DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD = -0.5', 'signature_specific_to_DDR' and 'MIN_GROUP_N = 5' each return one commit. No cut moved after the numbers landed. (The claim is verifiable as 'not changed since written', which is weaker than 'written before the numbers were seen'; the document says the former and calls it what makes the latter verifiable, which is a fair reading of what git can show.)

Every printed statistic I re-derived matches the committed artifact. Part C's six-gene table (ATR -1.386/-1.445/0.269/0.992/+1.23 and the other five) is byte-consistent with per_gene; the joint z (-0.0475 vs +0.0134, t -0.41), the quartile fractions (1/20 = 0.05 vs 3/71 = 0.042), the axis pool mean -1.340, the delta -0.0065 and the SD 0.1904 all reproduce — and 0.1904 is a real separately computed field (knockout_instrument_with_matched_comparator.axis_sd_sarcoma_pool), not, as it first appears, ATM's panel SD of 0.1901. Part D's seven-drug family and all four predictor rows reproduce exactly. Part B's GPL3290 and GPL6244 deltas and t reproduce to the printed precision, including the two the appendix records as previously transposed.

§5's self-audit is unusually strict and I could not break any of it: '+0.2123 clears it by 0.0155, 0.41x that standard error' is right (bar = 1.15 x 0.1711 = 0.19677; SE of a rho at n ~ 700 is 1/sqrt(697) = 0.0379, and for Spearman marginally larger, which only shrinks the margin further); 'no interval is computed anywhere in this analysis' is true; the signed-vs-absolute control-mean disclosure is right (mean_abs_rho_across_non_DDR_controls = 0.1589-0.2029 on the expression rows against signed means near zero); and the observation that the paper's own proliferation control is graded atri_specific: true is correct and is a genuine catch against its own instrument.

§6.1's one-sidedness catch is correct and is the sharpest thing in the document: 'mean_delta > 0.2' is one-sided upward, and an ATM-defect signature, whose predicted direction is down, could not register on that predicate however strong it was. Confirmed in code (ddr_up_raw / ddr_up_adj / ctrl_up all use '> 0.2').

§3.4's reference-channel confound is stated in the honest form — EMC and DFSP against CRH, GIST against UHR, 'group and reference pool are partly collinear', 'the direction of that bias is not determined here'. So is 'Part B's nulls are at n = 10 and n = 6 EMC tumours and no minimum detectable effect was computed, so their agreement is consistency between two underpowered reads, not a demonstration that a DDR signal is absent.'

Part C's two bias statements are both correctly signed. A fusion-caller miss puts a FET-positive line in the comparator and biases toward the null, and the paper says so and says the contrast is at the null already. The bottom-quartile-on-all-three null is the comparator's own fraction rather than 0.25^3, with the correct reason (the three genes are one module and correlated by construction, so independence would flatter the hypothesis).

§8.3 is the one place a control is defined so that it could fail, and it is done properly — absolute pre-specified cuts and a CANNOT_DETERMINE branch behind them. Its index confound is real and correctly handled: the family fraction NR4A3/(NR4A1+NR4A2+NR4A3) = 13.33/210.11 = 0.0634 reproduces, rank 29 of 68 against a median of 0.0524 is consistent, and 'Expression can raise or lower a suspicion; it can never close one' is the right strength at n = 1.

§2 keeps 'we did not find' and 'there is not' apart cleanly, including the load-bearing distinction between a reading of absence (ACH-001519 IS in OmicsFusionFiltered with 2 calls, neither naming a FET gene) and an absent reading (a model missing from the file). The '83rd percentile against a panel median of 0.214 is not high expression' caution is right, and 'Weak corroboration only' is the correct grade for it.

The proliferation-adjustment collinearity is disclosed with recomputed overlap fractions (ATR-CHK1 9/37 = 24.3 %, S-phase 54/200 = 27.0 %, checkpoint 68/200 = 34.0 % against 2.0-6.5 % for the unrelated controls), including the sharp part — 'the adjustment therefore partly subtracts these sets from themselves, and does so hardest for the three concepts it decides'. I could not find a stronger statement of that limit than the one already printed.

The 'none survives the proliferation adjustment' claim is NOT cleared by a margin smaller than its error, which is the failure mode I looked hardest for. _verdict_note: not_supported_as_written, on two blockers, both of which are single-sentence over-reads sitting on top of computations I could not break. Every number I re-derived from the committed artifact matched, the pre-registration claim in §1 is verifiable and true, and the document's self-audits are more severe than anything I found by looking for the usual failures — the passing test's 0.41-SE margin, the one-sided elevation cut, the reference-channel collinearity and the two-underpowered-reads caveat are all already printed, correctly, and at full strength. What fails is the join: in the two places where the document summarises rather than measures — the headline and §6.1's closing paragraph — instrument-limited nulls are promoted to evidence against the hypothesis. §6.1 counts a readout §4 says cannot refute, and a transcript proxy for an event §6.1 itself says no expression matrix can measure, as two of three 'bounds'; the headline reports the mechanism's load-bearing prediction as coming back with the wrong sign when what came back is a proxy that cannot see the variable. Both are of the exact class the document was built to prevent (§3.3's absent reading versus measured null, and the NOT_ASSESSABLE tier), applied rigorously to part B and not to parts C and D. The crux of this lens — transfer by class — is otherwise handled better than I expected: the banner states it, §6.2.1 states it, and the structural-precondition strand is correctly labelled eligibility rather than membership. The two places it slips are §8.2/§8.4's 'as its class is measured to be' (P1-4, contradicted by §8.5 in the same section) and §0's 'structural arguments from sequence' covering the RGG dose-calibration prediction (P2-6), which is a class transfer through other fusions' measured recruitment data. No verdict, tier or number in the document needs to change to fix any of this.
